title: Configurable embedding dimension end-to-end (migrations + HNSW honor :embedding_dimensions)
priority_note: THE self-host blocker. A user's agent correctly identified that the hardcoded vector(1536) prevents self-hosting with a local embedding model (nomic-embed 768, bge 1024, etc.). The Elixir validation layer ALREADY reads a configurable :embedding_dimensions; only the DB schema/index doesn't honor it. Unblocking this is the prerequisite for any local-embedding privacy story.

background.reference: config/config.exs:16 sets `embedding_dimensions: 1536`. validate_embedding_dimensions/1 already reads Application.get_env(:loopctl, :embedding_dimensions, 1536) in lib/loopctl/knowledge/article.ex:490 and lib/loopctl/memory/memory.ex:266. BUT the columns are hardcoded: articles `ALTER TABLE articles ADD COLUMN embedding vector(1536)` (20260410022854_enable_pgvector_and_add_embedding.exs:25); memories `ALTER TABLE memories ADD COLUMN embedding vector(1536)` (20260709000000_create_memory_stores.exs:101); HNSW indexes built on those fixed-dim columns (lib/loopctl/repo/hnsw_index.ex, 20260709000100/300). So on a fresh self-host, a 768-dim local vector fails to insert.
background.includes: Deployment-level dimension (one dim per instance) — sufficient for a single-org private self-host. Per-TENANT dimension (mixing dims in one HNSW column is impossible) is OUT OF SCOPE / deferred. Changing dim on an existing populated instance requires re-embedding + reindex — a documented one-time setup step, NOT an online migration.

story.as_a: someone self-hosting loopctl with a local embedding model
story.i_want_to: set the embedding vector dimension for my instance via config so the DB columns and HNSW indexes are created at that dimension
story.so_that: I can run knowledge + memory embeddings against a local OpenAI-compatible model (768/1024/etc.) instead of being forced to OpenAI's 1536-dim model

rationale: The app already treats the dimension as configurable everywhere EXCEPT the schema. Making the vector-column and HNSW-index creation read the same :embedding_dimensions config closes the gap with no behavior change for the default (1536) instance, and unblocks the entire local/private tier. It's the smallest change with the largest sovereignty payoff.

acceptance_criteria.description: The articles.embedding and memories.embedding vector columns and their HNSW indexes are created at the dimension from Application.get_env(:loopctl, :embedding_dimensions) (default 1536). On a FRESH database with :embedding_dimensions set to e.g. 768, the columns are vector(768) and a 768-dim embedding inserts + kNN-searches successfully. On the default (1536) instance, schema is byte-identical to today (regression test).

The configured dimension is the single source of truth: the migration/setup path, validate_embedding_dimensions/1 (article + memory), and any hardcoded 1536 literals in the vector path all resolve from :embedding_dimensions. A test asserts no code path assumes 1536 when the config differs (grep-guard test or a config-override test that exercises insert+recall at a non-1536 dim).

Changing the dimension on an EXISTING instance is handled safely: the system detects a mismatch (configured dim != column dim) at boot and fails loud with a clear, actionable message (re-embed + reindex required) rather than silently corrupting/rejecting inserts. A documented mix task or runbook performs the re-embed+reindex. This story does NOT auto-migrate existing data.

Purely enables a config; no default change. Hosted loopctl.com (1536, OpenAI) is unaffected. Documented in docs/agent-memory.md / a new docs/self-hosting.md: how to set the dimension for a local model.

test_cases.name: fresh DB at 768 dim round-trips
expected_results: insert succeeds; nearest-neighbour returns the row

test_cases.name: default 1536 schema unchanged
expected_results: vector(1536) as today; existing dimension tests pass

test_cases.name: dim mismatch fails loud at boot
expected_results: clear error naming the mismatch + remediation; no silent corruption

technical_notes: Files: priv/repo/migrations (the vector-column creation — parameterize the dimension from config; a fresh install reads :embedding_dimensions), lib/loopctl/repo/hnsw_index.ex (index dim), config/config.exs + config/runtime.exs (EMBEDDING_DIMENSION env → :embedding_dimensions), a new boot check + a re-embed/reindex mix task, docs/self-hosting.md.

pgvector: `vector(N)` column type is fixed per column; HNSW index inherits it. Migrations must interpolate N from config at run time (Ecto migrations can read Application env). For an existing 1536 instance the migration is a no-op; the dimension is only chosen at fresh install.
Do NOT attempt per-tenant dimensions (impossible in one HNSW column) — deployment-level only; note per-tenant as future work.
Re-embed+reindex on dim change is offline/one-time (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY the new, re-run embedding workers) — documented, not automated here.
Config-based DI; no Application.put_env in tests (use config/test overrides or a scoped helper).
